text:
maria: hey — my local sample app is flaking on event-stream responses. after the client reconnects, the server sends a few chunks but the client sometimes applies them out of order and the UI shows duplicate partial messages. logs pasted below.
maria: logs: 
```
[2026-06-15T14:02:01.123Z] connection established, id=abc123
[2026-06-15T14:02:02.456Z] chunk seq=1 token_count=45
[2026-06-15T14:02:02.789Z] client disconnected: ECONNRESET
[2026-06-15T14:02:03.001Z] reconnect accepted, resume_id=abc123 rseq=1
[2026-06-15T14:02:03.200Z] chunk seq=3 token_count=12
[2026-06-15T14:02:03.350Z] chunk seq=2 token_count=20
[2026-06-15T14:02:03.500Z] chunk seq=3 (duplicate)
```
maria: repro steps: run sample-app with `npm run demo`, trigger a 1.2k token response, then flip network in devtools. happens ~40% of attempts.
sam: ugh. curious — is your client reassembling by `last-event-id` or using an internal sequence? which SDK version?
maria: using our browser-sdk v0.9.7 (dev build). client stores fragments by `chunk.seq` from the `data` payload. i see two odd things: 1) seq=3 showing up before seq=2 sometimes, 2) duplicate seq=3. the server runtime should be strictly increasing. i can try to capture raw frames.
kelsey: pinging infra: could be two things: auth refresh creating a new connection that races with old in-flight frames, or our proxy doing HTTP/2 multiplex reorder when concurrent requests share the same connection. do you see `Last-Event-ID` or resume tokens changing?
maria: resume_id stayed `abc123`. no Last-Event-ID header in the reconnect request. i think client is not sending `Last-Event-ID` on resume, so server is trying best-effort resume and replays the tail. sample-app code uses this fetch snippet:
```
const res = await fetch(url, { headers: { Authorization: `Bearer ${token}` } });
const reader = res.body.getReader();
// naive: just push chunks as they arrive
while(true) { const { done, value } = await reader.read(); if(done) break; handleChunk(value); }
```
maria: i attempted a quick patch to persist the last event id and set `Last-Event-ID` on reconnect; that reduced duplicates but ordering still flips sometimes.
sam: can you share the exact wire-level SSE lines? we need to know if the server emits `id: <n>` lines for every chunk. also which proxy (nginx / envoy) in your local dev flow?
maria: emitting `id:` per-chunk, yes. local dev uses `http-proxy-middleware` (node) -> it proxies to our staging runtime. i grabbed a raw tcp capture; looks like two HTTP/1.1 requests overlapped briefly: one hanging socket then a second reconnect. server emitted chunks on both sockets before it noticed the old one closed.
kelsey: that makes sense. root cause could be: server treats reconnect as new connection immediately and emits the remainder on both connections while it backfills to the resumed socket. or proxy isn't draining the old socket so both get data. actionable: 1) client must send `Last-Event-ID` (resume point) on reconnect; 2) client should de-dupe by (id, payload hash) for safety; 3) server should avoid sending the same chunk on both sockets once it detects resume from a new connection.
sam: agree. also add a short reconnect backoff + jitter to reduce overlapping reconns — prevents the race when auth refresh kicks in twice.
maria: patch queued: i will update sample-app to store last `id` and send `Last-Event-ID`, add a small LRU to drop duplicate ids, and bump SDK to v0.9.8-dev. i'll paste PR link when ready.
dev-bot: CI pipeline: sample-app-ci #652 succeeded (tests: 124 passed) :tada:
maria: thanks — opening a follow-up issue to track server-side mitigation so runtime team can add server guardrails. tagging @kelsey for infra follow-through.
kelsey: thanks, pls include the tcp capture and proxy config in the issue. i'll file infra ticket after i review the logs. :thumbsup:
